City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Agency, Community Development Financing Authority, Public Improvement Corporation, and Library Board of Trustees*
December 4, 2006
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, Community Development Agency, Community Development Financing Authority, Public Improvement Corporation, and Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor MacLean at 05:04 p.m. , on December 4, 2006, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on December 01, 2006, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
CALL TO ORDER—CITY COUNCIL, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AGENCY, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT FINANCING AUTHORITY, PUBLIC IMPROVEMENT CORPORATION, AND LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES

Council Member Kelley
Council Member Ledesma
Council Member Reavis
Mayor Pro Tempore Ury

None

Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services
William P. Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
RECESS
At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor MacLean declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

City Clerk Karen Hamman administered the Oath of Office to Trish Kelley. Sarah Ledesma administered the Oath to her husband, John Paul Ledesma and Elissa MacLean administered the Oath to her son, Lance MacLean.
RECESS
At the hour of 6:34 p.m., Mayor MacLean declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:40 p.m., with all five Council Members present.

Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor MacLean, approve the First Amendment to Agreement with Securtec District Patrol, Inc., in the amount of $21,600.00.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Ledesma, Council Member Reavis, Mayor Pro Tempore Ury, and Mayor MacLean

ABSENT:

14.
Parking Restrictions on Camden (0870-20)
Transportation Manager Shirley Land presented the staff report.
Kyle Brownfield, Board Member for the Auburn Ridge Community Association, M.V.: presented photographs depiciting parking on Camden and expressed concern with the recommendation to remove parking restrictions.
Sivone Kalmanov, M.V.: stated that his property backs up to Camden and that he finds flaws associated with the proposal to remove parking restrictions.
Steve Dibble, M.V.: expressed support for the proposed removal of parking restrictions on Camden.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor MacLean, to Adopt Resolution 06-82 to Remove Parking Restrictions on Camden and direct staff to carefully watch this situation and bring it back to the City Council if necessary.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reavis, and Mayor MacLean
NOES:
Council Member Ledesma, and Mayor Pro Tempore Ury
ABSENT:
None
16.
Audit Report on Internal Controls Over Investments (0310-10)

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor MacLean, receive and file the report.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Ledesma, Council Member Reavis, Mayor Pro Tempore Ury, and Mayor MacLean

ABSENT:
None
PUBLIC HEARINGS
21.
Appeal of Architectural Review AR2006-91 Filed by Council Member Gail Reavis of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s October 23, 2006 Conditional Approval of a Petition Submitted by Shannon Craycraft to Add a 1,181sq. ft., Two Story Addition to the Existing 1,380 sq. ft. Dwelling, for a Total of 2,561 sq. ft. at 26632 Fresno Drive, in the RPD 3.5 (Residential Planned Development) Zone. The proposed Addition Consists of a 109 sq. ft. First Floor Addition and a 1,072 sq. ft. Second Floor Addition. Also Proposed is 528 sq. ft. of New Deck Area. The Appeal Petition Relates to Review of Conditions of Approval Placed on the Proposed Project by the Planning and Transportation Commission (0600-40)
Council Member Ledesma stated that he would recuse himself from participating in this discussion due to a personal bias. At the hour of 7:26 p.m., Council Member Ledesma vacated the dais.
Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.
Greg Craycraft, M.V.: addressed the four conditions that the Planning Commission placed on their project, addressed the objections from neighbor David and Jeanette Phillips, and outlined his plans for the home remodel/addition.
The following spoke in opposition to the proposed addition at 26632 Fresno Drive: David Phillips, M.V. and Jim Machulda, M.V.
The following presented written comments in opposition to the project: George and Patty Roberts, M.V.: Suzie Gaus, M.V.; and Jeanette Phillips, M.V.
Motion made by Council Member Reavis, seconded by Mayor MacLean, to Adopt Resolution 06-86 Approving Appeal of Architectural Review AR2006-91 Submitted By Shannon Craycraft for a 109 Square Foot (sf) First Story and a 1,072 sf. Second Story Addition to an Existing 1,380 sf. Dwelling in the RPD 3.5 (Residential Planned Development) Zone. Changes to Condition 1 are noted as follows: (1) the proposed rear deck will not be permitted and the door for the rear second story bedroom will be removed from the construction plan and replaced with a window, and (2) the property owners, the Craycrafts, shall provide and maintain landscaping which will create an obscuring effect to the adjacent property.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reavis, Mayor Pro Tempore Ury, and Mayor MacLean
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Ledesma
Council Member Ledesma returned to the dais at 8:15 p.m.
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORT
22.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report (0410-40)
Received the report from Council Member Kelley.
23.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report (0410-40)

City Manager’s Report

2007-2009 Budget Calendar and Master Financial Plan/Long Range Goals Workshop (0330-70)

Council Member Kelley, Council Member Ledesma, Council Member Reavis, Mayor Pro Tempore Ury, and Mayor MacLean

None
City Attorney’s Report
Announced that the Foothill Eastern Corridor Agency is engaging his firm, Richards Watson and Gershon, to assist in the Coastal Commission processing of the corridor extension. Wished everyone a wonderful holiday season.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS
25A.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended (AB 1234) (0480-70)
The City Council Members acknowledged the acuracy of their event and activities calendar as presented in the staff report. Council Member Reavis noted that she will provide amendments to her Calendar for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Congratulated the Capistrano Valley High School Marching Band Black and Gold Brigade for winning the Southern California Band Orchestra Association’s Division 1 Competition and announced that the Brigade also took first place in percussion scoring. Reminded residents that Santa Claus will be in his workshop at La Paz and Chrisanta every Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. Asked members of the public who are interested in becoming involved with the Mission Viejo Activities Committee to give them a call. Announced that she was unable to attend the Capistrano Unified School District’s recent meeting regarding the funding of the CUSD district building and that she is disturbed to hear that the City has been misinformed on this matter. Asked staff to look into an item that was included in the July 21, 2004, Arroyo Vista EIR regarding capacity at Newhart Middle School. Stated that she will be placing an item on the Agenda in January to discuss the recent addition of 300 students at the school and the impact this presents to the City and to the school's neighbors. Outlined a letter she received from B’Nai Brith offering to develop affordable senior housing in Mission Viejo. Requested that staff meet with representatives of B’Nai Brith to study the information and see what we can do to proceed with the offer and to hopefully address some of the City’s affordable housing requirements. Thanked the volunteers who serve the City through various committee memberships and announced that the Community of Character word for the month of December is caring.
Council Member Ledesma
Thanked the City’s residents for re-electing him to the City Council and wished everyone happy holidays and happy New Year.
Council Member Reavis
Thanked her colleagues for appointing her as Mayor next year and stated that Mayor MacLean will be a tough act to follow. Announced that she has been appointed to the League of Cities Senior Citizen Advisory Council and she invited residents to attend the Advisory Council's next meeting in the Saddleback Room at Mission Viejo City hall on Friday, December 8, 2006. In order to make sure that the City is not negatively impacted, she asked staff to conduct a full EIR on the conversion of Hankey School to K-8th grade. Stated that she has submitted her ideas on affordable housing to staff and she looks forward to seeing the City move forward with affordable housing matters next year. Reminded residents that the deadline for applications for appointment to a City Commission are due in the City Clerk's office by Monday, December 18, 2006. Wished everyone happy holidays and a happy New Year.
Mayor Pro Tempore Ury
26.
Brief Update on OCTA MIS Study (0840-30)
Received the update from Mayor Pro Tempore Ury.
Mayor MacLean
Referred to a letter he received from a contractor regarding the efficient and personal service he received from the City’s Building Services Department and Mayor MacLean stated that he feels fortunate to have such capable staff working for the City. Reminded residents to submit applications if they are interested in serving on a City Commission. Thanked the residents for re-electing him to the City Council and stated that he looks forward to representing his constituents’ views during the next four years. Thanked his colleagues for their support while he served as Mayor this year and wished everyone a safe and happy holiday.
ADJOURNMENT TO JANUARY 2, 2007, AT 5:00 P.M.
At the hour of 8:47 p.m., Mayor MacLean adjourned the meeting in memory of Monsignor John Francis Sammon, to Tuesday, January 2, 2007, at 5:00 p.m.

Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of January 02, 2007
